# Large-change response tuning

Historical Task 7 status: BLOCKED. The original eight-arm round selected no candidate because every arm failed the unchanged Quality textured-grain guard and at least one frozen rim gate. The Task 7b orchestrator amendment below selects arm 3 while keeping both residual gates RED for owner review.

## Method and unchanged gates

Device: MetalNative on Apple M2 Max, device class hardware. Each fixed arm ran once through the heavy build-slot lane after its own successful Release build. Every selected GPU fact executed with KE_GPU_TESTS=1 and KE_GRAPHICS_BACKEND=metal-native. There were no skips, repeats, cross-products, timing tests, stress runs or hosted dispatches.

The signed change is d = current qualified visibility mean minus previous qualified visibility mean. Lock release stays strictly abs(d) > 0.1. Current and previous depth qualification stays 0.02 * max(referenceDepth, 1e-5). A qualifying large change retains the stated scale of accumulated history weight and independently the same scale of the display share that would otherwise be used. The existing shading release still overrides both to zero.

The paired bilinear-only control leaves visibility history unseeded each frame while retaining valid colour history, the same input scene, light hold, jitter and original non-visibility resolve. It uses the existing test-visible renderer and test-only reflection on the visibility seed. The helper asserts comparison readiness is zero and colour history remains valid. Its eight exact tail values are identical in all eight arms and reproduce the frozen Task 3 four-decimal tail output. No reference, tolerance or frozen rim row was replaced.

Absolute 8 px textured and flat tails must not exceed that paired control plus the existing 0.0000005 rounding unit. The 1.5 fast/slow ratio and all moving, pan, band-grain and rim gates remain. Rim bounds are (frozen value + 0.0000005) * 1.1. Reference tolerance remains 0.000001. Native textured grain is bounded by 0.0113 and Quality by 0.008. Balanced remains report-only.

Archive context only: old unset Native advancing/retreating 8 px tails were 0.004441862 / 0.006978498 and archive reset values were 0.003520131 / 0.004718931. They are not portable bounds or the matched bilinear control.

No simplest passing policy exists in this candidate set. Every arm measures Quality grain 0.008031 against 0.008000. Even the closest rim choices retain the Quality M 1 leading textured miss. The round stops here and requires an owner-approved design amendment. Release-only remains an intermediate Task 6 state and is not shippable.

The release-only run also supplies behavioral RED for the new symmetric-reset contract. Its four rendered step tests expected confidence 1/15 but observed 1. The two carried-lock tests with no ridge and the strict response probe also failed that unimplemented reset contract. Its other three failed facts are the actual grain, rim and absolute-tail gates. Arm 1 has one additional fixture failure from comparing an exact zero with the pre-existing probe retention sink's 2e-29. That comparison was corrected to a 1e-7 float readback tolerance for subsequent arms. Neither fixture detail changes any grain, rim or tail bound. No arm was remeasured.

The corrected strict-boundary probe covers both signs at the threshold, adjacent floats below and above it, and unit changes. Rendered fused and split entry tests verify accumulation scaling once. Partial scale 0.25 produces confidence about 0.3166667 and scale 0.5 about 0.5666667 in the uniform large-step fixture, rather than either a full reset or unchanged accumulation. Existing independent shading release remains separate. The temporary experiment contracts and all candidate production code are removed after rejection.

### Response contracts and format boundary

Behavioral RED ran before implementation. Both rising entry cases retained confidence 1 instead of the expected 1/15. Both falling cases passed. After implementation, all nine focused response cases pass. Both entries store confidence 0.06665039 for a rising unit step, versus the scalar 0.06666667, and 1 for a falling unit step. The upscaled rising result is exactly the fresh resolve's colour, with no display share. The falling result is exactly the unchanged-history control's colour. The unchanged-history and fresh controls differ, proving that the display test exercises an active share.

The full-float probe checks both signs at 0.5, the adjacent floats on each side, and unit steps. Positive 0.50000006 and 1 retain scale 0, read back as the existing layout-retention sink's 2e-29 within 1e-7. Positive 0.5 and every falling boundary retain scale 1. Invalid footprints retain scale 1.

The single measurement executed 34 facts, with 31 passed, 3 failed and zero skipped. Two failed facts are the expected grain guard and rim gate. The additional failure exposed the old R8/R32 fixture's assumption that only the 0.1 lock-release boundary could change output. R8 rounds input 0.5 to byte 128, or 0.5019608, while R32 retains 0.5. Both release locks, but only R8 now resets history. Its colour maximum difference is 0.23852539, so exact output equality at that boundary is incorrect under arm 3.

The fixture now pins both scalar response decisions, includes the neighbouring R8 conversion boundary, requires observable colour/state differences when either decision differs, and still requires exact colour/state equality when both decisions agree. The corrected fixture passes its focused rerun, 1/1 with zero skips. No production source changed after the measurement. The full measurement filter was not repeated. This preserves the raw 31/3/0 result rather than presenting a rerun or a synthetic 32/2/0 aggregate as a measured run.
